propositions: Operators need an on-demand, non-blocking diagnostic to verify that mapped Jira project keys and legacy_default in .bridge_state/projects.json are visible to the bot outside a full reconcile pass.
The new --live-visibility flag on rebar bridge fsck must gate an opt-in, read-only, advisory live visibility check that reuses the shared check_mapped_project_visibility helper from ticket D.

When JIRA credentials (JIRA_URL, JIRA_USER, JIRA_API_TOKEN) are present, the fsck step calls the probe and reports visible/not-visible keys to stderr; when credentials are absent and no test probe is injected, the step emits a skipped advisory without calling the probe and without altering the exit code.
The default rebar bridge fsck output (no --live-visibility flag) must remain byte-identical with unchanged bridge_fsck.schema.json contract, as the advisory verdict is written only to stderr.

The live visibility check must live only on the bridge fsck surface and must not introduce new Jira dependencies into core rebar doctor (src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py) or add a new bridge doctor verb.
